strengths: FALCON addresses a meaningful problem: preserving previous segmentation knowledge while improving minority-class performance and learning useful representations of future classes. Combining persistent class centroids with learned cluster assignment is a potentially useful contribution to continual semantic segmentation.

The empirical evaluation is substantial, covering ADE20K, Pascal VOC, and Cityscapes, multiple incremental schedules, and convolutional and Transformer backbones. Reported gains include 62.41 versus 59.25 mIoU for SSUL on VOC 10-1 and 55.24 versus 49.22 for FairCL on Cityscapes 1-1.

The ablations provide evidence of practical benefits. In Table 1, the fairness loss improves minority-class mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 on ADE20K 100-50 while improving majority-class performance from 51.5 to 52.1, reducing the group gap. Table 4 also supports updating the visual grammar model rather than keeping its pretrained parameters fixed.

The supplement provides useful implementation details, a training algorithm, and sensitivity studies for the scaling factor, cluster margin, neighborhood size, and backbone. The discussion candidly acknowledges limitations in cluster initialization and continuity across learning stages.
weaknesses: The cluster regularizer has an unresolved optimization inconsistency. Equation (8) optimizes the segmentation parameters, but R_C depends only on cluster centers. These centers are described as frozen or updated periodically by momentum; supplementary Section 4 explicitly treats them as fixed during loss computation. Under that procedure, R_C has zero gradient with respect to the segmentation parameters. Consequently, its reported 1.3–1.5 point improvements in Table 3 require an unstated dependency or update mechanism. This affects the reproducibility of the central method.

Equation (4) does not clearly specify whether the learnable transition vector v participates in the softmax denominator. Proposition 2 requires a normalization that includes its probability mass. If the denominator contains only pixel features, as the preceding definition suggests, increasing v's projection onto its center makes the objective unbounded below. The distinction changes the objective fundamentally and must be resolved to assess technical correctness.

The theoretical fairness argument does not establish the claimed geometric effect. The optimum l_i = 1/L describes normalized probability allocation; a smaller value caused by having more samples does not imply a more compact cluster. Features with very different spatial dispersion can have identical projections onto a centroid and identical loss values. Similarly, reducing differences between these probabilities through alpha does not prove improved class fairness. The supplementary distillation argument also applies a triangle inequality without establishing that the actual contrastive loss is a metric, so Equations (16)–(17) do not establish the claimed bound.

The evidence does not fully isolate the unknown-class contribution. Section 4.2 states that removing visual grammar also changes the number of unknown clusters to one, confounding learned assignment with simply representing multiple unknown clusters. Figure 6 provides qualitative embedding evidence, but no quantitative unknown-cluster purity or assignment accuracy is reported. Since the attention model explicitly adopts Clusformer [35], controlled comparisons with the same cluster initialization and cluster count would also clarify the originality and benefit of the adaptation.

Fairness attribution and reproduction remain incomplete. The fairness loss is compared primarily with vanilla contrastive clustering, without comparisons to the cited parametric/balanced contrastive approaches or standard class-balancing losses. Aggregate majority/minority means cannot establish benefits across individual rare classes. Essential implementation choices—including DBSCAN parameters, visual-grammar pretraining construction and schedule, and conversion of unknown-cluster assignments into segmentation targets—are insufficiently specified. These reporting and evaluation limitations are secondary to the objective inconsistencies and unsupported theoretical claims, which outweigh the substantial experimental merits and determine my Weak Reject recommendation.
